page.layout: One page of text. At the top: page number and running title "CANTICVM", with two lines of verse above a rule. Below the rule: the heading "TERTIA PARS." centred, then the verse poem in one block with a large initial S, and the catchword "Cum" at the lower right. Show-through from the reverse page appears faintly in the right margin and is not transcribed.

p.i: Cunctis splendidius principium quae tribubus dedit:
Quae seruare solet terribilis robore brachij.
SED orbe toto facta qui mortalium
Sic ergo patrem me benignum degener
Sic, sic pudendum impura fertur ad nefas,
Sed ecce densa nube posthac abditus
Quae me parentem foederis sacri immemor
At illa poenas criminis pares suo
Aegreque cernet amula, ut meum nova

page.notes: The large initial S is joined to the word "SED". The reading "Quae" in the running head line is printed Quæ. Verse lines are each given as their own paragraph, as printed. Nothing is marked [?]; all readings are clear on the scan.
